title: Bidirectional BFS: Find the Way Across Valparaíso!
description: Watch Bidirectional BFS visually “meet in the middle” as two BFS frontiers expand from start and goal across Valparaíso’s steep, winding street graph. The first collision point reveals the shortest path in an unweighted map model.
ig_caption:
🚠✨ Valparaíso (Cerro Alegre) navigation, but make it graph theory.

In this visualization, **Bidirectional BFS** runs two simultaneous BFS waves: one forward from the start node and one backward from the goal node. Each layer expands in increasing distance, so when the frontiers **collide**, you’ve found the shortest route on an **unweighted street graph**—typically faster than a single BFS because the search space shrinks from roughly O(b^d) to about O(b^(d/2)).

🗺️ Street maps become graphs: **intersections = nodes**, **road segments = edges**, and travel constraints are baked into edge connectivity. As the waves expand, you can literally see the algorithm “compress” the problem until the meeting point stitches together the optimal path.
